---
title: Synthetic Data
related:
  - Supervised Fine-Tuning
  - Evaluation
  - Prompt Engineering
  - Knowledge Distillation
---
**Synthetic data** is generated by models or simulators for training or eval—e.g., LLM-written instruction pairs, rewritten documents, or simulated tool traces.

It scales labeling when human annotation is slow or expensive, and it can target rare edge cases. The risk: it amplifies teacher biases, style quirks, and [hallucinations](/ai-glossary/hallucination/). A student trained only on a teacher’s outputs may never exceed the teacher on factual ground truth.

### Hygiene
- Filter for format, toxicity, and factuality where possible
- Mix synthetic with real domain text when available
- Hold out *real* eval sets; never grade only on synthetic twins of the train set
- Prefer diverse teachers and templates over one prompt repeated forever

Synthetic SFT corpora and [knowledge distillation](/ai-glossary/knowledge-distillation/) pipelines are closely related: both treat a stronger model as a noisy labeler.
